name: Nha Trang food guide
summary: The provincial digital guide names nem nướng and bún cá from Ninh Hòa, bánh căn, and the Trần Phú night market. The provincial tourism department names the bowls and the dried counter at Chợ Xóm Mới. A Ministry of Culture reprint of Báo Khánh Hòa names a longer Khánh Hòa list, including gỏi cá mai and bánh canh cá dầm. The restaurant names further down are doors, not a ranking.
body: Start with the two Ninh Hòa names. Nem nướng is the grilled pork roll. Bún cá is the fish bowl, morning or evening. Bánh căn is the clay-mold rice cake. The provincial digital guide puts squid, shrimp, or egg on it, at the night market behind 46 Trần Phú and again along Tháp Bà in the late afternoon.
The doors further down come from the provincial digital guide, the provincial tourism department, and Vietnam Tourism. Check on arrival. A room with no dish named stays a name.

A Ministry of Culture reprint of Báo Khánh Hòa names the longer Khánh Hòa list, from gỏi cá mai in Nha Trang to tôm hùm Bình Ba and bánh tráng xoài Cam Lâm. Where that reprint gives no recipe, the dish is still named. Check on arrival.
specialtiesLead: Highlights, in source order: nem nướng, bún cá Ninh Hòa, bánh căn, the night-market stalls, the six chè bowls, the Chợ Xóm Mới bowls, yến sào, the Khánh Hòa dishes a Báo Khánh Hòa reprint names, and the market specialties at Chợ Xóm Mới and Chợ Đầm.
seoTitle: Nha Trang food — nem nướng, bún cá, bún sứa, and the markets
seoDescription: Nha Trang specialties from the provincial digital guide and a Báo Khánh Hòa list: nem nướng, bún cá, bánh căn, bún sứa, gỏi cá mai, and the market counters.

sections.heading: Specialties
paragraphs: These are the dishes to know by name. Nem nướng is the grilled pork roll from Ninh Hòa. Bún cá is the fish bowl, morning or evening. Bánh căn is the clay-mold rice cake, with squid, shrimp, or egg.

Night-market stalls, from the provincial digital guide: bún chả, chả cá, bánh căn, fried squid, breaded shrimp, ice cream, pomelo chè, sương sa hạt lựu chè, ginseng chè, green-bean chè, glutinous rice balls in syrup, and lotus-seed chè.

Chợ Xóm Mới, 49 Ngô Gia Tự, names bánh canh chả cá, bánh xèo, bún sứa, nem nướng, bún chả cá, bún cá, bún canh, chè, and bánh. Chợ Đầm names bún cá, bún chả cá, and nem, plus bánh tráng, muối ớt xanh, and mắm. Yến sào is the nest product: Hòn Nội from the tourism bureau, Yến Island from Vietnam Tourism.

A Ministry of Culture reprint of Báo Khánh Hòa, 6 Sep 2023, names nem chua with nem nướng, vịt lội Ninh Hòa, tôm hùm Bình Ba, nai khô Diên Khánh, cá tràu Võ Cạnh, sò huyết Thủy Triều, bánh ướt Diên Khánh, lẩu mực Đại Lãnh, bánh canh hẹ Vạn Giã, gỏi cá mai Nha Trang, bánh canh cá dầm Nha Trang, bánh tráng xoài Cam Lâm, and bún mực Vạn Ninh. It also prints bún lá cá dầm Ninh Hòa and bánh canh chả cá Ninh Hòa, which stay the bowls already named. The dried counter at Chợ Xóm Mới names mực một nắng, mực rim, cá khô, and cua rang muối. A recipe for those lines was not printed. Check on arrival.

spots.name: Nem nướng
spots.note: Grilled pork paste from Ninh Hòa. The provincial digital guide describes skewers, bánh tráng phơi sương, herbs, pickles, fried ram, and a yellow-orange sauce of lean pork, liver, shrimp, sticky rice, and fermented bean.

spots.name: Bún cá Ninh Hòa
spots.note: Fish noodle bowl. Body text: cá thu, cá ngừ, and cá cờ. Caption: cá dầm usually from cá bò and cá ngừ. Broth of fish bone, pineapple, and tomato. Cake from cá đỏ, cá nhồng, and cá thu ảo. Morning and evening. A Ministry of Culture reprint of Báo Khánh Hòa also prints the name bún lá cá dầm Ninh Hòa and does not give a second recipe, so it stays this bowl. No Nha Trang street is printed.

spots.name: Bánh căn
spots.note: Rice soaked overnight, poured thin into a clay mold with no oil. The provincial digital guide puts a quail egg, fresh squid, or a whole shrimp on the batter, and names plates of chicken or quail egg, mực lá, shrimp, and minced beef, plus fried shallot and scallion oil. Dips on that article: sweet-sour fish sauce, mắm nêm, or salty-sweet nước mắm cá kho, with scallion oil, pork xíu mại, and chopped mango. A street-snack article on the same site says the coastal cake, unlike the Đà Lạt cake with xíu mại broth, is topped with fresh squid, shrimp, or egg, and dipped in sweet-sour fish sauce, nước cá kho tót, and scallion oil. Both accounts stay. Night market behind 46 Trần Phú, and late afternoon along Tháp Bà. That street article also names the Phan Rang market, which is not a Nha Trang address. Check on arrival.

spots.name: Bún sứa
spots.note: Jellyfish noodle bowl, morning or afternoon. The provincial article says the broth is sea-fish bone, not pork bone: cá thu, cá cờ, or cá liệt, with ripe tomato. In the bowl: offshore jellyfish, fried fish cake, steamed fish cake, cá dầm, lettuce, chopped banana blossom, and bean sprouts, plus nước mắm ớt xanh. Add a little mắm tôm or mắm ruốc, depending on the shop, and lime. A street-snack article says the breakfast broth is cá cờ bone and cá dầm. Both stay. The provincial tourism department names the bowl at Chợ Xóm Mới. Check on arrival.

spots.name: Yến sào
spots.note: Swiftlet nests. Hòn Nội from the tourism bureau, Yến Island from Vietnam Tourism. Products named: raw nests, cleaned nests, and nest drinks, including Sanest. A Ministry of Culture reprint of Báo Khánh Hòa says unnamed old books describe a cooled cup of thoroughly cooked nest between about 8 and 9 in the evening, after lying down around 7, then a rinse with warm water. That is not a current shop hour. Check on arrival.

spots.name: Nem chua Ninh Hòa
spots.note: Named with nem nướng on a Ministry of Culture reprint of Báo Khánh Hòa, 6 Sep 2023. That paragraph’s story of nem Ninh Hòa is lean pork pounded and wrapped in lá chùm ruột, sour and sweet, later with garlic, and a dip the reprint says was wanted both sweet and hot. The reprint does not say which of the two names the story belongs to. A shop was not named. Check on arrival.

sections.heading: International dining
paragraphs: These doors are the foreign and chain rooms the provincial tourism department names. Vinpearl Harbour names Kohaku Ramen and Nướng Quảng Châu. Vincom Plaza Trần Phú names King BBQ and Hotpot Story. Vincom Plaza Lê Thánh Tôn names Master Beef, Gogi House, Jollibee, Sumo BBQ, Alfresco, Salsa Express, and Uber. Nha Trang Center names Haidilao, KFC, and Texas Chicken. Where only the sign is named, a dish was not added.

sections.heading: Fine dining
paragraphs: The provincial digital guide prints one steak room it calls cao cấp: Ember Steakhouse at 16A Trần Phú. The plates the provincial digital guide names are that room’s dishes, not separate restaurants.

spots.name: Ember Steakhouse
spots.note: The provincial digital guide calls this a cao cấp steak room at 16A Trần Phú, phone 0398 537 968. Dishes it names: Ember Signature Tomahawk, Dry-Aged Ribeye, Wagyu Striploin, Surf & Turf Nha Trang, Fire Kissed Oyster, Seafood Grill Platter, and Truffle Mashed Potato. Wine is mentioned. Check on arrival.

sections.heading: Themed dining
paragraphs: Themed here means a room tied to a view, a floor, or a night setting. Vietnam Tourism names Sailing Club on the beach and Skylight on the 43rd floor of Havana Hotel. The provincial digital guide names Champa 76 for coffee at sunset. The provincial tourism department names Sunset Bar, Li’a Cuisine & Mixology Bar, Kasan Beer, and Warning Zone at Vinpearl Harbour. Wonder Club and The S Hookahs are late-night rooms there. Food at those two rooms was not named, so they are not dining entries.

sections.heading: Breakfast
paragraphs: Kubera serves a breakfast buffet for guests at Champa Island. Champa 76 also serves breakfast. Bún cá is also eaten from early morning. A city breakfast street, with a clock, was not printed.

spots.name: Kubera
spots.note: The provincial digital guide says Nhà hàng Kubera serves the breakfast buffet for guests staying at Champa Island. It sits by the river at 304 đường 2/4.
